metadata.title: PISA 2022 Results Volume III: Creative Minds, Creative Schools Factsheets Baku (Azerbaijan)

survey_design.weight_fields_interpretation: This factsheet reports PISA 2022 creative thinking results for Baku (Azerbaijan) using OECD’s PISA 2022 Database. The document does not specify whether student/sampling weights or replicate weights were applied in the production of the reported estimates. For PISA analyses, analysts should use the provided sampling weights (and replicate weights if variance estimation is required) to account for the complex two-stage sampling design and clustering of students within schools. Because this is a descriptive results factsheet rather than a re-estimation study, the manuscript does not report any custom weighting variable names or replicate procedures.

data.handling_not_reported_explanation: This factsheet is a descriptive reporting of PISA 2022 creative thinking proficiency and related breakdowns (e.g., mean scores, proficiency levels, and correlations) rather than an empirical model that re-estimates achievement using PV-based regression. The dependent quantities shown are presented as PISA results on a 60-point scale and proficiency levels, but the factsheet does not document the PV combination or missing-data strategy used to compute those published estimates. Therefore, missing-data handling is not reported in the provided text, and PV handling is treated as not applicable for this extraction because no PV estimation procedure is described.

sample_details.sample_filtering_criteria: The factsheet reports that, in Baku (Azerbaijan), 7,720 students in 178 schools completed the assessment in mathematics, reading or science, representing about 30,500 15-year-olds (about 73% of the total 15-year-old population). The text does not describe additional analytic exclusions (e.g., missing background questionnaire items) or further subsampling beyond the Baku implementation and the stated completion of the assessment.

data.outcome_summary: This OECD PISA 2022 Volume III factsheet reports creative thinking outcomes for 15-year-old students in Baku (Azerbaijan). The creative thinking test contains 32 open-ended tasks measuring three ideation processes (generating diverse ideas, generating creative ideas, and evaluating and improving ideas) across four domain contexts (written expression, visual expression, social problem solving, scientific problem solving). In Baku, the mean creative thinking score is 23 on a 60-point scale, significantly below the OECD average of 33. The factsheet also reports proficiency distribution (44% at Level 3 or above; 8% at Level 5 or 6) and relationships with mathematics and reading performance (correlations of 0.64 and 0.63, and 34% of creative thinking variance uniquely explained by mathematics). It further highlights within-Baku gaps by socio-economic status and gender, and notes COVID-19-related implementation cautions for some participating economies.
data.null_fields_interpretation: This document is a descriptive OECD factsheet summarizing published PISA 2022 results for a single participating location (Baku, Azerbaijan). It does not present an original student-level analytical model, machine learning procedure, or re-estimation strategy; consequently, there are no ML techniques to extract and no predictive/causal findings to tabulate. Several methodological details (e.g., PV combination and missing-data handling) are not included in the factsheet text, which is consistent with it being a results dissemination product rather than a methods paper.
